question: Which plan introduced Minimum Needs Programme?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fifth**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Minimum Needs Programme (MNP)** was introduced during **India’s **Fifth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974).
 
• The MNP aimed to improve the living standards of the poor by meeting their basic needs, including health, education, drinking water, rural roads, housing, and nutrition.
 
• It was considered a crucial step towards reducing regional disparities and fostering economic and social equity in India.
 
• The program targeted rural and underprivileged areas, emphasizing the creation of infrastructure and provision of basic services.
 
• The MNP became a core component of national planning and was implemented in subsequent Five-Year Plans as well.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Third Five-Year Plan (1961-1966):**

 
 
• The focus of the Third Plan was on **self-reliance and economic stability**.
 
• It prioritized agriculture and aimed to achieve a target of 5% growth in national income.
 
• However, the plan faced challenges due to the Sino-Indian War (1962), droughts, and economic instability, which led to its underperformance.
 
 
 
• **Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-1979):**
 
 
• The Fifth Plan emphasized **poverty alleviation (Garibi Hatao)** and self-reliance in the Indian economy.
 
• The plan introduced major initiatives like the **Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP)**.
 
• It also focused on increasing employment opportunities and enhancing agricultural productivity.
 
 
 
• **Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-1985):**
 
 
• This plan marked the beginning of **economic liberalization** in India.
 
• It focused on **poverty eradication, technological development, and modernization of industries**.
 
• Programs like the National Rural Employment Programme (NREP) were introduced during this period.
 
 
 
• **Minimum Needs Programme (MNP):**
 
 
• The MNP was a significant initiative to address basic needs such as education, healthcare, and infrastructure, particularly in rural areas.
 
• Its goal was to ensure equitable distribution of resources and balanced regional development.
 
• Over time, the program evolved and merged with other schemes to enhance its reach and effectiveness.
